title: Mutations in SLC6A19, encoding B0AT1, cause Hartnup disorder
authors: Kleta R, Romeo E, Ristic Z, Ohura T, Stuart C, Arcos-Burgos M, et al.
population: Members of the original family in which Hartnup disorder was described in 1956 and of three Japanese families
funder: Grants-in-aid from the Japanese Government to A.K. and Swiss National Science Foundation grants to F.V.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing financial interests.
result: Hartnup disorder, autosomal recessive, results from impaired neutral amino acid transport across epithelial cells of renal proximal tubules and intestinal mucosa; symptoms include transient pellagra-like rashes, cerebellar ataxia and psychosis. Mutations in SLC6A19 were identified in the original 1956 family and in three Japanese families; its product B0AT1 is expressed mainly in intestine and renal proximal tubule and functions as a neutral amino acid transporter.
